answer: Coordinated-Kernel Spacing Rule. Each new identity must solve a per-epoch puzzle whose difficulty is derived from a shared kernel of recent activity, so batches of identities face rising cost as they grow. Joining also requires a quartz-timestamped delay, forcing attackers to spread registrations across time. Admission consumes a river of scarce epoch slots, priced by congestion. A sybil swarm thus pays superlinear compute plus scheduling latency per identity.
